issue.title: Bug: 'config interface ip add' adds entries for non-existent intefaces

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

`config interface ip add` does not check to see if the interface string that is passed to it corresponds to a valid interface. It will accept arbitrary interface names and will add misformed entries for these invalid interfaces to ConfigDB. These entries cannot be removed by `config interface ip delete` because that command checks the actual interface list, and these entries are never present there. Trying to run `config replace` fails because these bad entries do not pass yang validation.

### Steps to Reproduce

Trivial to reproduce.

Run the command and pass an interface name which matches the basic pattern for a routed interface, but does not exist, for instance:

`sudo config interface ip add EthernetNotARealInterface <IP>`

The command will complete and return success. An entry will be added to the VLAN_SUB_INTERFACE table, using the invalid interface name as the key. Running `sudo config replace /etc/sonic/config_db.json` at this point will fail, since the added entry will fail yang validation.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual Behavior:

```
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config interface ip add EthernetNR <IP>
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config interface ip add EthernetJustMadeUp <IP>
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config interface ip add Ethernet99999999 <IP>
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config interface ip add Ethernet-totally-not-real <IP>
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config interface ip remove EthernetNR <IP>
Cannot find device "EthernetNR"
admin@gold113-dut:~$ sudo config replace -d /etc/sonic/config_db.json
** DRY RUN EXECUTION **
Config Replacer: Config replacement starting.
Config Replacer: Target config length: 50412.
Config Replacer: Getting current config db.
Config Replacer: Generating patch between target config and current config db.
Config Replacer: Applying patch using 'Patch Applier'.
Patch Applier: localhost: Patch application starting.
Patch Applier: localhost: Patch: [{"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/EthernetJustMadeUp"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/Ethernet-totally-not-real"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/EthernetNR"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/Ethernet99999999"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/EthernetJustMadeUp|<IP>~132"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/Ethernet99999999|<IP>~132"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/Ethernet-totally-not-real|<IP>~132"}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/INTERFACE/EthernetNR|<IP>~132"}]
Patch Applier: localhost getting current config db.
Patch Applier: localhost: simulating the target full config after applying the patch.
Patch Applier: localhost: validating all JsonPatch operations are permitted on the specified fields
Patch Applier: localhost: validating target config does not have empty tables,
                            since they do not show up in ConfigDb.
Patch Applier: localhost: sorting patch updates.
Failed to replace config
Usage: config replace [OPTIONS] TARGET_FILE_PATH
Try "config replace -h" for help.

Error: Data Loading Failed
Leafref "/sonic-port:sonic-port/sonic-port:PORT/sonic-port:PORT_LIST/sonic-port:name" of value "EthernetNR" points to a non-existing leaf.
```

Expected Behavior:

Command is not accepted, no bad entries are added to ConfigDB

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell
Seems to be a day-1 issue, present in all versions which support this command.
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: Issue #22759: Prevent CLI from adding invalid routed interfaces
resolution.description:
#### What I did

Currently, config interface ip add will accept EthernetX interfaces which do not have an underlying port or portchannel associated with them. This violates the yang model, so if these entries are added to ConfigDB, 'config replace' and 'config reload' don't work properly. To make matters worse, the implementation of config interface ip remove does not detect these invalid entries, so once they are added they cannot be removed through the CLI. I modified the command to reject invalid cases.

Fixes: [#22759](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22759)

#### How I did it

Add a check for this case into the config interface ip add CLI command to avoid invalid cases of this form by checking to ensure that the interface which is passed is associated with a valid port or port channel if it is an Ethernet or PortChannel interface. There is already an existing check for vlan interfaces.

#### How to verify it

Modify existing test cases to handle expected behavior, verify that they all pass.
